call_points.text: Management expects significant inventory and debt reduction over coming quarters as BSNL order executes.
Company reconfirmed visible path to profitability in upcoming years.
Q3FY27 will see significant cash collections from BSNL tied to achieved delivery milestones.
Total global patent count increased to 748, with 266 focused on 5G Advanced and 6G standards.
First end-to-end 5G network win in South America, including radios, baseband and core, is in the order book.
5G massive MIMO radios supplied to a global customer in partnership with NEC; Tejas is NEC's preferred radio partner.
Net receivables rose to ₹2,232 Cr from ₹1,905 Cr; management expects BSNL receivables to clear during the quarter.
Inventory fell to ₹2,358 Cr from ₹2,438 Cr; management says the build was advance procurement for add-on orders.
Warranty provisions rose because of the large BSNL rollout; management calls it one-off and expects normalisation.
BSNL AMC revenues, higher margin, start after acceptance and warranty and run over 8 years, circle by circle.
New TJ1600-D3 data centre interconnect product is in initial customer engagements and field trials this year.
6G commercialisation expected around 2030, with product launches probably in 2029.
Management targets a financial turnaround starting in FY27, aiming for breakeven.
Intangibles under development rose to ₹960 Cr, including product development and NEC technology licensing.
Significant BSNL collections are expected during FY27, which should reduce receivables.
Signed agreement with NEC to supply 5G Massive MIMO radios for a global customer.
Revenue shortfall in FY26 was primarily due to delays in large customer projects.
Total headcount remained stable at approximately 2,300 employees.
Received ₹69 Cr in PLI incentives for FY25, totaling ₹469 Cr for the year.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Excise Department had issued an order directing the inclusion of software value in hardware for the purpose of calculating excise duty, resulting in a demand of Rs. 42.93 crores. Tejas Networks had challenged this order by filing an appeal before the Honorable CESTAT, Chennai. Subsequently, Civil Appeal No. 011078 was filed before the Honorable Supreme Court during September 2018, and the same is currently pending. The case has been listed for hearing via video conferencing. The Advocate-on-Record has been informed to request a physical hearing. No further updates have been received from the Supreme Court at this time. Separately, the Department filed an application for early hearing before the CESTAT, which was disallowed on 22nd October 2021.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Department of Central Excise and Service tax
tax_litigation.status: There has been no further development in the matter during the quarter October - December 2025

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: A writ petition No.11707/2025 was filed by the Company on 15th April 2025 before the Honorable High Court of Karnataka, challenging the Order-in-Original No. 582/2024-25 AP and ACC dated 13.01.2025. The Honorable High Court has on 21st April 2025, granted an interim stay against the the order of Commissioner of Customs.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Principal Commissioner of Customs , ACC, Bangalore

International 5G orders carry no performance-linked payment conditions and follow standard 60-90 day payment terms.
Warranty provisions dropped to ₹7.24 Cr in Q2FY27 compared to ₹35.11 Cr in Q1FY27 and ₹44.44 Cr in Q2FY26.
Trade receivables reduced by ₹1,099.64 Cr in H1FY27, supporting cash flow against operating losses.

Q2FY27: global patent count increased to 748.

Q2FY27 order book stands at ₹2,315 Cr (96% India, 4% International).

timeline.summary: Tejas Networks reported a widened FY26 PAT loss of ₹909 Cr on revenue of ₹1,103 Cr, while its order book grew to ₹1,514 Cr.
Tejas Networks signed an MoU with MahaIT to jointly impart training in emerging telecom technologies across Maharashtra.

Q1FY27 (Jul 2026): Tejas reported revenue of ₹402 Cr, up 21% QoQ, a PBT loss of ₹271 Cr, an order book of ₹1,529 Cr and net debt of ₹4,277 Cr, with the BSNL 26,000-site add-on order still in final stages of award.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹405.68 Cr (+54.9% YoY), net loss ₹206.94 Cr (against a loss of ₹307.13 Cr a year earlier).

Q2FY27 (Oct 2026): Tejas reported revenue of ₹406 Cr; a net loss of ₹207 Cr; order book of ₹2,315 Cr (+51% QoQ) and net debt of ₹4,384 Cr; it received a TCS LoI for 4G RAN at 18,865 BSNL add-on sites and a BharatNet Phase 3 IP router LoI.
Anantha Murthy Narayana, Chairman, shared the Q2 FY27 earnings call recording link on October 16, 2026, available at tejasnetworks.com.
Tejas Networks reported Q2FY27 order book of ₹2,315 Cr and outlined plans for significant inventory liquidation and debt reduction as BSNL 4G expansion order execution scales up.
